paper_metadata.title: Quantum Algorithms for Solving Large-Scale Optimization Problems: Challenges and Breakthroughs

summary: The paper presents a hybrid variational optimization framework centered on QAOA and VQE for benchmark problems including Max-Cut and Travelling Salesman, reporting convergence in about 30–40 iterations and robustness up to 100 qubits. It claims superior performance over classical heuristics for instances larger than 50 variables and an order-of-magnitude gain in accuracy and computational efficiency, but does not provide exact numerical benchmark values.

experiments.description: Hybrid gate-based quantum-classical optimization framework evaluated on benchmark combinatorial and convex problems using QAOA and VQE, with comparisons against classical heuristics.

algorithm.convergence_criteria: until convergence is achieved; convergence shown around iterations 30–40

problem_formulation.objective_function: Minimize expectation value of cost Hamiltonian <H_C> for combinatorial/convex optimization problems
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: Penalty terms implied through Hamiltonian encoding; hybrid classical optimization loop
problem_formulation.problem_hamiltonian: H_C = sum_{<i,j> in E} w_ij (1 - Z_i Z_j)/2
